newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd rebel chief seeks Western pressure on Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Kurd rebel chief seeks Western pressure on Turkey.

text.p: The leader of a Kurdish rebel group called on Western countries to pressure Turkey into bringing its anti-guerrilla operation in northern Iraq to an end, a pro-Kurdish television channel said on Monday.
Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) chief Abdullah Ocalan was quoted by pro-Kurdish MED-TV, based in Belgium, as warning the West of the consequences if it did not pressure Turkey.

"We can hold to a unilateral ceasefire or political dialogue. But if they say 'no, it must continue like this', we cannot be held responsible for the consequences," Ocalan told a panel programme by telephone on Sunday evening.

Ocalan, whose forces are fighting for independence or autonomy from Turkey, is believed to be living in the Syrian-controlled Bekaa valley of Lebanon. A transcript of his remarks was made available to Reuters on Monday.
PKK rebels have in the past attacked Turkish businesses and offices in European countries as well as in Turkish holiday resorts.

Turkey's big assault against PKK bases in northern Iraq, now in its sixth day, has drawn fire from western capitals and the United Nations, who have urged Ankara to withdraw and expressed concern for the safety of civilians.
Meanwhile, military sources reported fresh fighting in eastern Turkey.
According to official figures, more than 23,000 people have died in the PKK'S 12-year-old insurgency, including more than 1,000 in the current northern Iraq operation.
